daily_quests.title: ASX 200 Price Momentum Ranking with Window Functions
daily_quests.description: Using the ASX 200 historical prices dataset, write a SQL query with window functions to rank stocks by their 30-day price momentum. Calculate the percentage change from 30 days ago to today for each stock using LAG() and RANK() functions. Include columns: stock_symbol, current_price, price_30_days_ago, momentum_pct, momentum_rank. Filter only for stocks with valid 30-day history and order by momentum_rank. Use a CTE to calculate lagged prices, then a second CTE to compute momentum percentages.

daily_quests.title: NSW Road Crash Data Cleaning & Aggregation Pipeline
daily_quests.description: Download NSW Road Crash Data (CSV format). Write a Python script using pandas to: (1) Load the dataset and identify missing values and inconsistent data types; (2) Clean the crash_severity column by standardizing values (e.g., 'Fatal', 'Serious injury', 'Other injury'); (3) Parse date columns into datetime format; (4) Remove duplicate crash records based on crash_id; (5) Create a new column for crash_hour extracted from time data; (6) Aggregate crashes by local government area (LGA) and severity, counting total incidents; (7) Export cleaned data to a new CSV file with summary statistics printed to console (total crashes, crashes by severity, top 5 LGAs by incident count).
daily_quests.dataset: NSW Road Crash Data — Transport for NSW (data.nsw.gov.au)

daily_quests.title: Melbourne Pedestrian Hourly Footfall Analysis & Anomaly Detection
daily_quests.description: Combine Python and SQL to analyze Melbourne pedestrian counting data. (1) In Python: Load the pedestrian CSV dataset, clean datetime columns, handle missing sensor readings, and aggregate hourly footfall counts by sensor location. Save to a SQL database (SQLite). (2) In SQL: Write a query using window functions (AVG() OVER, ROW_NUMBER()) to calculate the 7-day rolling average of hourly footfall for each sensor. Identify anomaly_hours where current hourly count deviates by more than 2 standard deviations from the rolling average. (3) Export results showing sensor_id, timestamp, actual_count, rolling_avg_7day, anomaly_flag, and anomaly_severity. Expected output: 100-500 flagged anomaly records representing unusual pedestrian patterns.
daily_quests.dataset: Melbourne Pedestrian Counting System — Melbourne Open Data Portal
